question: Which acid is produced by the human stomach?
solution:
The correct answer is __**HCl.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hydrochloric Acid:**

 
 
• The **human stomach produces HCl** as part of the gastric juice.
 
• It **helps break down food,** particularly proteins, and creates an acidic environment that is essential for the activation of enzymes involved in digestion.
 
• The **stomach lining has protective mechanisms** to prevent the acid from damaging the stomach itself.
 
• It is produced by specialized cells in the stomach lining called parietal cells.
 
• It is primarily **used to denature proteins,** which increases their susceptibility to **enzymatic digestion.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lactic Acid:**

 
 
• It is** classified as a hydroxy acid** and is a carboxylic acid with the **chemical formula C₃H₆O₃.**
 
• It exists in** two optical isomers**: L-lactic acid and D-lactic acid.
 
• The accumulation of lactic acid in muscles is often associated with **muscle fatigue and soreness**, particularly during strenuous exercise.
 
• It serves as an acidulant,** flavoring agent, and preservative** in various products.
 
 
 
• Acetic Acid:
 
 
• The chemical compound acetic acid has the formula CH3COOH.
 
• It is a carboxylic acid with a carboxyl functional group joined to a methyl group.
 
• The presence of acetic acid is evident in its strong aroma and tart flavour.
 
• When the temperature drops below 16.6ºC, it produces crystals that resemble ice.
 
• Vinegar, commonly known as acetic acid or ethanoic acid, is a common culinary and laboratory reagent.
 
• The bacteria Acetobacter aceti is the source of it.
 
• Methanol is carbonylated in an industrial setting to make acetic acid.
 
 
 
• **Sulphuric Acid:**
 
 
• Mineral acids having the chemical formula **H₂SO₄** are sulfuric acid.
 
• Other names for sulfuric acid include **Mattling acid and Oil of Vitriol.**
 
• It is** corrosive and has a strong acidic tendency**.
 
• It functions as an **oxidising and dehydrating agent** at greater doses.
 
• It is a **colourless, syrup-like liquid with no smell.**
